original_test_intent: Orderly shut down the intended powered-on SUT through the BMC Web UI and prove clean OS/workload/storage quiescence, chassis off/standby transition and absence of unexpected new errors.
original_method: Verify target and on state, drain workloads and storage, preserve baseline, issue one documented Web UI graceful-shutdown or approved equivalent request, monitor OS/console/chassis completion and compare post-shutdown events.
manual_activity: The owner approves the outage, defines orderly semantics and final state, confirms workload/storage drain and recovery; an operator supervises the shutdown and retains authority over any escalation.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/BMC and verified powered-on state
Owner outage approval and expected off/standby state
Supported BMC Web UI graceful action or documented OS/Redfish equivalent
Clean workload, storage and firmware-update state
Shutdown completion signals, timeout and event acceptance rule
safety_requirements: Drain workloads and storage and reject active firmware operations
Do not substitute immediate chassis off, reset or AC removal
Protect credentials and verify the management endpoint
Preserve event baseline before any log handling
Issue one graceful request and monitor real completion
Stop on continuing writes, partial shutdown, timeout or unexpected error
Do not escalate or auto-retry without separate approval
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, on state, approval and clean drain gates
Preserve pre-shutdown device, storage, health and event baseline
Monitor OS, console, storage, BMC and chassis until the defined final state
Compare new errors and preserve evidence without force-off, recovery autonomy or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve outage, graceful semantics, timeout and final state
Supervise shutdown and authorize any separate escalation

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Inapplicable: CRPS SDR/sensor reads belong to duplicate row 787 and cannot request or verify orderly shutdown; the SSH construction is also secret-unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the documented Web UI graceful-shutdown action or approved equivalent once, with protected credentials and real OS/chassis monitoring.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Orderly Web UI power-off, no-error criteria, private scripts and 1/15-minute fields are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a target-on-drain-baseline-single-graceful-request-completion-event sequence with bounded monitoring.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Clarifies graceful versus immediate action and adds workload/storage drain, secure control, timeout and recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Static sensor visibility cannot establish shutdown request, OS quiescence, chassis state or clean events.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A failed graceful shutdown may leave service partially stopped; force-off can corrupt data and is outside this case without new approval.

project_override_considerations: The project may use Web UI, Redfish or an OS shutdown interface only if it documents graceful semantic equivalence; immediate off, reset or AC removal remains uncovered and cannot be used as fallback evidence.
expected_evidence: Approval, target identity, on state and clean workload/storage/update assessment
Immutable pre-shutdown device, storage, health and event baseline
OS service, storage-drain, console and chassis-state transition timeline
Final off/standby state and BMC reachability
Post-shutdown event comparison, recovery actions if any and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Row 1509 consistently defines orderly BMC Web UI power-off. The reused-code row 787 is isolated by Source Key and variant as a dual-CRPS thermal case.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The supported graceful interface, approval, drain and timeout rules are finite normal inputs; once supplied, attended execution is feasible.

review_improvement: Rejects the copied CRPS sensor path and defines a one-request graceful shutdown with workload/storage safety, authoritative completion and error-event evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Orderly shutdown is defined by software quiescence and the intended chassis final state, not by sensor readability. Because it interrupts service and may require human escalation if it stalls, execution remains conditional and supervised even though request and monitoring steps can be automated.
